title: Fable du Souffle
identity: Jean-René Combes-Damiens, Fable du Souffle (1990), Leduc AL28154, for alto saxophone and piano, c. 3 minutes. The opened French Wind Music Archive item identifies a four-page score plus one part, elementary level 1 as printed on the score, and Année 4 in the archive index. A Philharmonie de Paris repertoire guide describes the contrasting slow/fast sections; that is guide commentary, not notation inspection.

evidence.claim: Search result identifies AL28154, E-flat saxophone and piano, Collection Rougeron; one listing shows 96 pages, likely a pagination anomaly requiring checking against the physical score.

Philharmonie repertoire-guide entry describes a tranquil 6/8 and 3/4 opening, a faster cheerful contrasting passage with tempo changes, then a return to slow material an octave lower. This is descriptive guide text; no notation was inspected.
evidence.source_name: Philharmonie de Paris, 10 ans avec le saxophone

evidence.claim: French Wind Music Archive item identifies the 1990 A. Leduc edition AL28154, four-page score plus one alto saxophone part, three minutes, “Niveau Élémentaire 1” noted on the score, and archive classification Année 4.

review_focus: The Philharmonie guide describes a shift between slow 6/8/3/4 material and a faster, tempo-changing dance, then a return an octave lower. If the score is obtained, check how this arc is realized in the saxophone part, especially octave change and transition timing.
collection_flag: Original alto saxophone and piano work per the archive’s bibliographic record. The archive describes the score as elementary level 1 and separately indexes it Année 4; the Philharmonie guide documents its repertoire use.

score_links.description: Opened archive bibliographic item page; no notation preview.

gaps: No actual score page or matching saxophone recording was inspected; the musical description comes from the repertoire guide, not direct notation review.
The archive’s Année 4 classification and score’s “Niveau Élémentaire 1” label use different systems and are not college-year recommendations.
